scope: bounded natural-language teaching instructions over the frozen parent world (END_TO_END_POC entities + STATUS + REPORT) and the frozen PROCEDURE_PRIMITIVES_V1 inventory. NOT open English.
supported_forms: simple conjunctions (and / then / and then / comma)
simple sequencing words (first, then, next, finally)
explicit example values (names, times, places, topics from the frozen vocabulary)
naming an ACTIVE procedure to call it
unsupported_forms: external-world actions (send, text, post, phone, print, browse, download ...)
unsupported_response: UNSUPPORTED_TEACHING_INPUT (nothing executes, nothing enters the trace)

domain_conventions.inner_time: The time of an inner event (CALL, EMAIL, VISIT, MESSAGE) is stored on the outer event that schedules it: 'calls at 3' = FIND CALL WHERE PARENT.WHEN=3. Encoded in the action grammar: for inner event types the only WHEN constraint offered is PARENT.WHEN.
domain_conventions.outer_scope: Outer events (REMINDER, PLAN, REQUEST, NOTE) carry their own WHEN/WHO; a constraint on their TODO item uses CHILD.<REL>.
domain_conventions.value_formatting: type-preserving formatting repair: 'H:00' -> 'H', 'H o'clock' -> 'H', case-insensitive vocabulary match (Alice / alice).

reference_grammar.candidates: prior results of the CURRENT demonstration only (bounded local trace context), filtered by the input type the chosen operation requires
rules_in_order: R4 (checked first, RETURN only) the instruction names result / type nouns but no type-compatible candidate matches any of them -> CLARIFY (the requested result has not been computed)
R0 exactly one type-compatible candidate -> that candidate
R1 the chosen candidate was produced earlier IN THE SAME instruction and is the most recent type-compatible result produced in it -> licensed
R2 the instruction (or its clarification answer) contains a type / result noun that matches exactly one type-compatible candidate -> that candidate
R3 the instruction contains a singular pronoun (it / its / that / this) -> the most recent type-compatible singular (non-list) candidate
otherwise -> CLARIFY (a plural pronoun with >= 2 compatible lists is NEVER resolved by recency)
reference_grammar.repair: if the frontend chose a different candidate than the unique one licensed by R0/R2/R3, the licensed one is used (DETERMINISTIC_REPAIR, logged)

coverage_rule: every PERSON / TIME / PLACE vocabulary value mentioned in the instruction must be an argument of some grounded action; every literal argument must be a vocabulary value of its class that occurs in the instruction (TOPIC values are checked for occurrence only, since topic words such as 'report' are also ordinary nouns); ACTIVE procedure names mentioned in the instruction must be CALLed. A grounding that violates coverage is a CLARIFY outcome (it competes as a candidate; never executed)
parameterization: the frontend never decides parameters: concrete values enter the trace; the frozen anti-unifier decides parameter vs constant. UNHINTED one-shot teaching whose trace contains a PERSON / TIME / PLACE / TOPIC literal -> REQUIRE_SECOND_DEMONSTRATION
clarification: V1.1: a pending clarification is a record {kind: REFERENCE, source_utterance_id, instruction, unresolved_slot, legal_answers}. The next utterance consumes it ONLY if it names exactly one legal answer (a type / result noun or result name matching exactly one candidate); otherwise the record is cleared and the utterance is grounded as a new instruction. Low-margin / coverage / plan / segmentation CLARIFY ask for a rephrase and leave nothing pending.
correction: an utterance starting with a correction marker undoes the previous grounded instruction of this demonstration (world restored to its pre-instruction snapshot, its steps removed from the trace) and grounds the rest of the utterance instead; the undone proposal stays in provenance only
teaching_sandbox: every demonstration executes against the world, and at :endteach / :endexample / :endrevise the world is restored to the demonstration's start snapshot (teaching effects are discarded; procedures persist)
undo_command: :undo (undo the previous grounded instruction of the current demonstration)
status_rule: a FIND / FILTER status constraint is offered only if the instruction contains a status cue word (a word starting with one of status_cue_roots); the LLM then chooses OPEN / CLOSED / no status
return_rule: RETURN is always the last action of an instruction (nothing may follow it)
dangling_rule: every result produced by an instruction must be consumed by a later action of the same instruction, except the result of the instruction's last action; violating groundings are not candidates
sequencing_rule: V1.1: candidate segmentation. STRONG = explicit sequencing markers; FULL = strong + weak plain 'and'. Each clause is grounded to a NON-EXECUTABLE plan fragment (earlier clauses' planned results are in-instruction context for R1); the combined plan must pass whole-plan validation (liveness / DEAD_PURE_RESULT, value + named-procedure coverage, RETURN last, CLAUSE_COVERAGE = #actions >= #clauses). The finest segmentation that validates is chosen (a weak 'and' that does not yield valid clauses is not a clause boundary). The whole utterance is also grounded; if it validates, covers every clause and yields a DIFFERENT plan -> CLARIFY (segmentation uncertain). The whole-utterance fallback has the same authority: the same whole-plan validation with the strong clause count. Only the complete validated plan executes, as ONE transaction.
event_search_rule: V1.2: FIND / FIND_LAST are offered only if the instruction (clause) names an event type with a registered type noun, and only those types (no invented search)
antecedent_rule: V1.2: a clause containing an anaphor (antecedent_pronouns; relative 'that' and 'the ones' are not anaphors) must reference at least one existing result; groundings that do not are not candidates -> if none remains, CLARIFY. Together with event_search_rule no antecedent can be invented.
output_request_cues: \b(tell me|let me know)\b.*\b(how many|the number|the count|the total)\b
output_obligation_rule: V1.2: an utterance carrying an OUTPUT_REQUEST cue must be grounded to a plan whose last action is RETURN; the returned result must match the requested result kind when one is named (R4). Violating groundings are not candidates; the combined plan is checked again in whole-plan validation
